To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
most GPs are enthusiastic about their role in prevention but few are currently practising systematic screening for risk.

most general practitioners in Oxfordshire were enthusiastic about prevention, but that few were actively screening for risk factors in their patient populations and few had established a systematic approach to preventive health care.

(a) general practitioners' attitudes to their preventive role in health care were very positive; (b) few general practitioners claimed to discuss smoking, alcohol, diet or exercise as a matter of course with all their adult patient population; (c) few general practitioners maintained statistics on the prevalence of risk factors in the practice population; and (d) general practitioners' enthusiasm for their role was not matched by the adoption of systematic screening for risk factor and lifestyle advice.

general practitioners are enthusiastic about prevention and health promotion but are not yet systematically screening for risk factors or providing lifestyle advice for all their patients.
